answer: Proof-of-burn protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to destroy base cryptocurrency at an unspendable address before registration. The public burn transaction acts as an audit lantern, demanding irreversible liquid capital per identity so an adversary cannot scale this capital ridge to flood the market with an echo of cheap bots. A key limitation is that deep-pocketed adversaries can still register swarms whenever expected exploit profits exceed the burned capital.
